item.title: China's emerging, future industries achieve momentum via new blueprints
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
China's emerging, future industries achieve momentum via new blueprints Foreign tourists experience AI sports glasses at an INNO100 shop in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Aug. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- From intelligent connected new energy vehicles and biomanufacturing to quantum precision measurement, China is materializing its industrial ambitions with the guidance of a cluster of detailed five-year sector blueprints. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the country aims to speed up the development of strategic emerging industries while cultivating future industries as new growth drivers. These sector plans, together with national guidelines on new quality productive forces issued in October, provide a detailed framework for moving Chinese industry up the value chain. More than listing promising technologies, these plans identify how innovations will be led to production, and where new products can be applied. This is crucial to the next stage of China's high-quality development. ANCHORING FRONTIER TRACKS These sector-specific blueprints highlight sci-tech innovations, with advancing industrial modernization acting as the guiding principle. The five-year plan for electronic information manufacturing development issued in September clearly illustrates this approach. It calls for developing frontier electronic measurement technologies such as high-bandwidth, terahertz and quantum precision measurement. Motivated by this deployment, Ceyear Technologies Co., Ltd. has strengthened its technological research and launched a new generation of electronic measurement products, the performance of which, it says, matches advanced international standards. Its products, notably, already serve several strategic emerging industries like aerospace, satellite communications and AI. Similar priorities run through other plans, but with different industrial entry points. The plan for the pharmaceutical industry puts innovation first among eight major tasks, and identifies frontier technologies for basic research, technology transfer and industrial maturation. The plan for renewable energy development emphasizes frontier, original and disruptive technology research and equipment breakthroughs, while the green and low-carbon industry plan urges tackling key technologies for clean and low-carbon hydrogen, and speeding up the development and application of high-performance and degradable bio-based materials. These forward-looking measures could spark breakthroughs in frontier technologies needed to drive overall industrial upgrading, help China's industries move toward the middle and high ends of the global value chain, and strengthen their international competitiveness, said Deng Zhonghan, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering. BUILDING INDUSTRIALIZATION BRIDGES Selecting promising fields is only the first step. Hard-technology projects often require long investment cycles, while many research teams lack pilot facilities and first customers. The plans therefore seek to make companies central to innovation and connect research with industrial demand. Chinese enterprises already account for more than 75 percent of the country's total R&D spending for several consecutive years, making them the mainstay of sci-tech innovations. In Chongqing Municipality in southwest China, a biomanufacturing pilot platform offers a glimpse of such a bridge being built. Rows of reactors and purification equipment are undergoing process validation before production begins. Put into use in June 2026, this platform has signed up more than 20 research teams and enterprises, allowing them to test and refine processes without each having to build a full pilot line. "The pilot platform has addressed our urgent need in commercializing research results and significantly reduced R&D investment and trial costs," said Ou Zhen, director of the general manager's office at Hymos (Chongqing) Bioscience Co., Ltd., adding that the company has developed 17 types of recombinant human keratin and is advancing the commercialization of multiple keratin products with the platform's support. China's policy toolkit extends beyond shared facilities. Companies are encouraged to lead national science and technology tasks, while cross-sector innovation consortia can bring manufacturers, suppliers and researchers together. Universities and research institutes, meanwhile, are encouraged to license results to small and medium-sized enterprises on a "use first, pay later" basis. Talent and finance policies complete the support system, promoting closer industry-education integration and calling for more patient capital that invests early, in small companies, for the long term, and in hard technology. PROVIDING NEW OPPORTUNITIES The strategy is not confined to industries still in their infancy. The October guidelines specify support for upgrading traditional industries via digital, intelligent and green technologies, while identifying industries such as mining, metallurgy, chemicals, light industry, textiles, machinery, shipbuilding and construction. In a high-tech zone in Weifang, east China's Shandong Province, engines move along intelligent production lines at a Weichai Group workshop. From diesel engines to new energy, technological upgrade of this leading traditional power equipment maker illustrates how innovation can transform an established manufacturer, rather than simply replace old industries with new ones. This combination of new industries and modernized existing ones is key to the development of new quality productive forces. Frontier sectors can create fresh growth drivers, while a broader industrial base supplies components, engineering expertise and markets for their products. "The real test of new quality productive forces is not under the spotlight at a press conference, but in companies' actual financial statements," said Yan Yang, vice president of the Beijing Internet of Things Intelligent Technology Application Association. These plans also create potential entry points for international partners. The October guidelines call for a global innovation cooperation network, including joint science parks, Belt and Road joint laboratories, and international centers for applying advanced technologies. They encourage foreign venture-capital institutions and international standards organizations to develop in China, and call for efficient, convenient and secure cross-border data flows. Some foreign companies are already positioning themselves around the opportunities brought by China's emerging and future industries. Corning Incorporated is expanding optical-communications capacity in east China's Shanghai, and south China's Guangdong and Hainan, as the country's industrial digitalization increases demand for upstream materials. General Electric's energy investment arm in China, meanwhile, has joined China Huadian Corporation and Peking University's energy research institute in research on hydrogen applications. Such projects show how overseas technology, capital and expertise can connect with Chinese manufacturing, infrastructure and research capabilities. The guidelines urge local governments to adapt industries to local strengths, avoid blind investment and prevent "involution-style" competition. If these guardrails hold, the blueprints could turn a dispersed set of technology bets into a more coherent industrial pipeline, which will foster new growth engines, upgrade China's manufacturing foundation, and provide overseas partners with a clearer roadmap for initiating and advancing collaboration. item.title: World media leaders urge stronger oversight, inclusive cooperation amid AI-driven transformation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
World media leaders urge stronger oversight, inclusive cooperation amid AI-driven transformation BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the global media landscape, opening up new possibilities for media organizations to improve efficiency and reach wider audiences, while posing pressing challenges to journalistic integrity, human judgment and the future of the very profession. At the 7th World Media Summit, held in Beijing from Nov. 5 to 9, media professionals from around the world explored ways to better harness AI to improve news production while avoiding ethical pitfalls that could undermine trust in their content. They emphasized that embracing the technology must go hand in hand with upholding journalistic principles, and that international cooperation is essential to navigating the transformation. The summit, jointly organized by Xinhua News Agency and the Beijing municipal government under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action," brought together about 500 representatives from nearly 330 media organizations, think tanks, government bodies and international organizations across 112 countries and regions. "AUGMENTED JOURNALISM" AI is finding its way into virtually every stage of news production, from story planning, information gathering and processing to fact-checking, proofreading, and even the generation of news images and videos. Addressing the opening ceremony, Fu Hua, president of Xinhua News Agency, called on media professionals to share new technologies and applications, exchange experience in using them, and close gaps in AI research, development and understanding. "We should lead the way in ensuring that all media professionals have a fair chance to benefit from AI," he said. "Newsrooms everywhere are under pressure. Audiences expect faster coverage, more formats, more languages and more explanations," Agence France-Presse (AFP) Chairman and CEO Fabrice Fries told a high-level dialogue during the summit, which brought together executives from Xinhua News Agency, The Associated Press, Reuters, AFP and CNN. "AI can help us automate repetitive tasks, process large amounts of information, translate content more efficiently and support our journalists in their daily work," he said. The AFP chief described this approach as "augmented journalism," in which journalists spend less time on routine production and more time observing reality, meeting people, identifying emerging trends and explaining complex developments with greater depth and context. At the opening ceremony, Reuters President Paul Bascobert also mentioned AI as "a resource, a tool that increases speed, efficiency and scale" for journalists. "Those are real gains, but AI does not replace our standards. It has to meet them. We automate tasks. We do not automate judgment," he added. The world's first bionic humanoid robot news anchor makes its official debut at a sub-forum titled Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Chinese Modernization of the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 5, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Chenlin) During the summit, two life-sized robot news anchors, as the world's first bionic humanoid robot news anchors, made their official debut, greeting the audience in fluent English. "I heard about and saw AI anchors presenting news during my previous visit, which really impressed me," Sumeyra Teymur, CEO of Turkish news platform Haberler.com, told Xinhua ahead of the summit. She also expressed interest in the potential use of humanoid robots to cover dangerous situations, such as earthquakes and conflicts, where deploying human reporters could pose risks. Fu said that as AI technology advances, media practitioners should make good use of AI while safeguarding the credibility of mainstream media. "Xinhua is willing to strengthen dialogue with all parties to advance the industry's development and promote exchanges and cooperation," he told media executives at the high-level dialogue during the summit. A guest attending the 7th World Media Summit (WMS) views dexterous robotic hands at the Zhongguancun Exhibition Center in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Mao Zhu) TOOL VS HUMAN JUDGMENT AI is becoming increasingly embedded in the media industry, yet one message came through clearly in discussions among media representatives at the summit: it is a tool to assist journalists, not to replace them. Many speakers used the same word, "tool," to describe AI's role in news production. Toshimitsu Sawai, president of Japan's Kyodo News, said generative AI is an "assistive tool" for editorial work. However, he said, AI carries risks such as copyright infringement and the dissemination of misinformation and disinformation. He also noted cases triggered by "out-of-control behavior" by AI models. "Humans bear final decision-making authority and responsibility for content," Sawai said. "In this respect, it is increasingly important that professional journalists have a strong grasp of how to handle information and make judgments about news." In the same vein, CNN Senior Vice President Kostas Oikonomou said AI is "a tool to strengthen our reporting, not replace the human judgment that defines it." Bascobert of Reuters said that news delivery methods had evolved dramatically over the years, from carrier pigeons and telegraphs to today's digital technologies. "The tools have changed a great deal since then. The principle has not," he said, stressing that the core task of journalism remains getting the facts, checking them and reporting them. While AI is a valuable tool, Bascobert said, it cannot replace the human qualities that make a good journalist, including the ability to gain people's trust, read people, and understand nuances in conversation. "Whatever technology we adopt, we should never lose sight of the fact that the most important aspects of journalism are done by people," he said. Fries of AFP expressed optimism about the future of journalism, saying professional journalism becomes even more important in the future because it remains one of the few ways to maintain a direct connection with reality. "AI and journalism should not be viewed as rivals," he said. "They need one another. Our challenge is to build a future in which technological innovation and trustworthy information grow stronger together." For media organizations and journalists standing at the intersection of technology, information and public trust, Tatiana Valovaya, director-general of the United Nations Office at Geneva, highlighted three priorities: protecting information integrity and public trust; ensuring AI benefits everyone; and keeping human dignity and responsibility at the center. Guests attend the opening ceremony of the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 7, 2026. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong) COOPERATION FOR INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT While AI offers extraordinary opportunities, "it also presents serious challenges, from synthetic content and information manipulation to threats to privacy, algorithmic bias, and unequal access to technology," Valovaya said. "We believe international cooperation is essential," she said, emphasizing that AI's opportunities and risks are "too consequential to be left to a handful of countries or companies." Media representatives at the summit shared the view that no single organization could address these challenges alone. "International cooperation holds the key," said Sawai of Kyodo News, expressing hope that "discussions at this summit will deepen our collaboration and lead to a more informed, connected -- and peaceful world." In this evolving environment, collaboration between media companies is "a strategic necessity" to combine their respective strengths, create greater value and offer audiences a richer, more comprehensive view of the world, said Oikonomou of CNN. Strong partnerships also "create opportunities to learn from one another, embrace innovation and explore new ways of working across content, platforms and business models," he added. Guests attending the 7th World Media Summit (WMS) interact with a robot while visiting World of Robots in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong) A concrete step toward such cooperation came with the summit's release of the Global Media Initiative for the Joint Development of AI Application Standards on Saturday. Launched by Xinhua, the initiative brings together major media outlets and other professional organizations to safeguard the authenticity of information, protect data security, and uphold media ethics, thereby maintaining public trust in the media. Under this initiative, participants plan to work together for about two years to develop a set of standards that address different media uses of AI and are validated by media outlets. The initiative also calls for a global database of AI applications. Xinhua looks forward to further strengthening cooperation with fellow media organizations to promote closer people-to-people ties and play a positive and constructive role in advancing relations between countries, said Fu. Tanzanian media professionals attend a China-Africa AI media training program in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, Nov. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Emmanuel Herman) The need for inclusive media cooperation was also highlighted by representatives from the Global South. "We hope the initiative will become a practical avenue for cooperation, sharing expertise and building capacity, and media organizations of different sizes and with different resources can apply the standards," said Mohammed Alyami, director general of the Union of News Agencies of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, which is also among the first participants, in an interview with Xinhua. "International cooperation must therefore ensure that developing countries and small island states can contribute not only to AI's development, but also to the principles governing it," said Aminath Namza, chairperson of Public Service Media in the Maldives. Likewise, Wong Chun Wai, chairman of the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), called on Global South countries to work together more closely in the changing media landscape and ensure that media organizations worldwide can share in the benefits of AI. item.title: Second China-Canada Strategic Economic and Financial Dialogue concludes in Vancouver
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
Second China-Canada Strategic Economic and Financial Dialogue concludes in Vancouver VANCOUVER, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- The second China-Canada Strategic Economic and Financial Dialogue was held on Monday in Vancouver. He Lifeng, member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, vice premier of the State Council, and Chinese lead person for the dialogue, co-chaired it with Canadian lead persons Francois-Philippe Champagne, minister of finance, and Maninder Sidhu, minister of international trade. He stated that under the strategic guidance of the leaders of both countries, China-Canada relations have turned for the better, and bilateral exchanges have returned to a sound track. He said this dialogue is a concrete measure to implement the important consensus reached by the leaders of both countries, adding that China is willing to work with Canada, upholding the principles of mutual respect, equality, mutual benefit, and seeking common ground while reserving differences, to deepen cooperation in areas such as economy and trade, finance, and investment, promote the stable and healthy development of China-Canada economic relations, and contribute to building a new type of strategic partnership between the two countries. Champagne noted that Canada attaches great importance to its relations with China and is willing to work with the Chinese side to implement the consensus reached by the leaders of both countries, strengthen policy communication and coordination, and deepen mutually beneficial cooperation in the economic and financial fields. Sidhu said that Canada looks forward to further expanding practical cooperation with China in trade and economic sectors and driving greater development in bilateral economic and trade relations. During the dialogue, the two sides reached a series of mutually beneficial outcomes and consensus. He, Champagne, and Sidhu jointly attended a business roundtable with industry leaders from both countries to discuss opportunities to expand bilateral trade and investment on Sunday. item.title: China's foreign trade growth picks up pace on stellar imports, booming AI demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
China's foreign trade growth picks up pace on stellar imports, booming AI demand BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- China's foreign trade in goods maintained strong growth momentum in the first 10 months of 2026, with imports posting especially robust gains and booming artificial intelligence (AI) demand lifting exports of electronic components, official data showed Tuesday. Total imports and exports grew 20 percent year on year to 44.81 trillion yuan (about 6.67 trillion U.S. dollars) over the period, accelerating from 18.8 percent in the first nine months, according to the General Administration of Customs (GAC). Imports surged 23.6 percent, while exports rose 17.6 percent during the January-October period. China's foreign trade has kept up its momentum this year, showing greater resilience and vitality, said Lyu Daliang, director of the GAC's Department of Statistics and Analysis. Both imports and exports have now posted double-digit growth for six consecutive months through October, the customs data showed. In October alone, goods trade expanded 31.2 percent. Notably, imports have been a standout feature this year. "In the first 10 months, China's imports from more than 150 countries and regions recorded growth. Imports from ASEAN, Latin America and Africa all reached record highs for the same period," Lyu said. "China's vast market continued to offer 'China opportunities' to the world." On the export side, mechanical and electrical products played a prominent role with a 25.2 percent increase over the period, accounting for 64.7 percent of total exports, up 3.9 percentage points from a year earlier. Wang Qing, chief macro analyst at Golden Credit Rating, said multiple factors kept export growth elevated in October, noting that the global AI investment boom continued to push up prices of chips and other electronic components and computer parts, driving strong growth in export value. Moreover, domestic manufacturing upgrades in recent years have also enhanced the competitiveness of new energy vehicles and high-tech products, Wang said. Smart and green products were among the fastest-growing categories. Exports of integrated circuits and memory components surged 101.9 percent and 132.5 percent, respectively, while 3D printers, digital cameras and industrial robots rose 104.8 percent, 41.4 percent and 17.8 percent. Exports of China's "new three" -- electric vehicles, photovoltaic products and lithium batteries -- grew 46.5 percent, electric motorcycles and bicycles rose 33.3 percent, and wind turbines and their components gained 19.7 percent. By trading partner, China's trade with ASEAN grew 24.2 percent in the first 10 months, while trade with the European Union rose 8.5 percent and trade with the United States expanded 6.3 percent. Trade with Belt and Road participating countries grew 18.5 percent over the same period. Looking ahead, experts believe the strong exports will extend through to the end of the year. As the AI cycle remains in an upswing, China will continue to benefit as a global hub of electronics supply chains, Zhang Di, a macro analyst at China Galaxy Securities, said. The ongoing global green and low-carbon transition, combined with China's rising competitiveness in mechanical equipment, will sustain strong growth in new energy vehicles, ships and other transport machinery, Zhang added. item.title: Hairy crab industry thrives in E China's Jiangsu
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
Hairy crab industry thrives in E China's Jiangsu Farmers pack hairy crabs in Hongze district, Huai'an city, east China's Jiangsu Province. (People's Daily Online/Jiang Nan) Crab trading points in Xishunhe town, Hongze district, Huai'an city, east China's Jiangsu Province, are bustling as the peak season for hairy crabs gets underway. "This year, each mu (about 0.067 hectares) of pond is expected to yield at least 200 kilograms of hairy crabs," said Xuan Ankui, a sales manager at a local agricultural development company. Hongze Lake, China's fourth-largest freshwater lake, has consistently maintained water quality at Grade III or above. Mineral-rich soil and abundant natural feed around the lake provide favorable conditions for hairy crab farming. Yet limited farming techniques in the 1990s kept output low and the district's hairy crabs little known. "Raising crabs is not like growing crops. You can't see disease underwater, and if you spot it a little late, you could lose money," said crab farmer Zhang Lijun. Tourists enjoy hairy crabs at the 4th Hongze Lake Swimming Competition and Thousand-Person Crab Feast held by Hongze district, Huai'an city, east China's Jiangsu Province, on Oct. 18. (Photo/Yin Chao) In recent years, the district has built a wholesale market for aquatic products, a provincial-level hairy crab breeding farm and a provincial-level modern agriculture demonstration park. Smart equipment has been used for crab farming in the demonstration park since the park began operation last year. "In the past, we relied on experience. Now water temperature, dissolved oxygen and pH levels are clear at a glance," Zhang said, demonstrating how he monitors and manages his crab ponds using his phone. People take photos at the 4th Hongze Lake Swimming Competition and Thousand-Person Crab Feast held by Hongze district, Huai'an city, east China's Jiangsu Province, on Oct. 18. (Photo/Yin Chao) In the demonstration park, farming costs have fallen by 15 percent, while crab sizes have increased by 10 percent. This year, the district's crab farming area totals 39,000 mu, with output expected to reach 6,000 tonnes. The hairy crab industry in the district now provides employment for 16,000 people and generates a total output value of more than 3 billion yuan (about $450 million). Photo shows a provincial-level modern agriculture demonstration park in Hongze district, Huai'an city, east China's Jiangsu Province. (Photo/Yin Chao) Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China hands over remains of U.S. airmen found along WWII Hump Route
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
China hands over remains of U.S. airmen found along WWII Hump Route A transfer ceremony of the U.S. service members' remains along the Hump Route is held in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, Nov. 10, 2026. The Chinese and U.S. militaries on Tuesday held a ceremony in Chengdu where China handed over the remains of U.S. airmen who aided China's resistance against Japanese aggression during World War II (WWII), according to China's Ministry of National Defense. The remains were recovered in areas along the Hump Route, a vital air corridor over the Himalayas that became a wartime lifeline for China. From 1942 to 1945, the route served as a key channel for Allied supplies to support China's resistance against Japanese aggression. item.title: China's second homegrown large cruise ship starts first trial voyage
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
China's second homegrown large cruise ship starts first trial voyage This photo taken on Nov. 6, 2026 shows the cruise ship Adora Flora City at Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation Limited (CSSC), in Shanghai, east China. (Xinhua/Ding Ting) SHANGHAI, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- China's second domestically built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, departed from the Shanghai Wusongkou International Cruise Terminal in east China on Monday, starting its first trial voyage. The ship is scheduled to arrive at the Nansha International Cruise Home Port in Guangzhou, south China, on Nov. 12. This voyage is set to comprehensively test the cruise ship's operational capabilities, marking a key step toward formal commercial operation. During the voyage, systematic tests and adjustments will be carried out in areas including maritime operations, navigation safety, products and services, ship-shore coordination, and ship-wide information systems, according to the operator. Under simulated real operating conditions, stress tests will also be conducted on core guest experiences such as cabin service, dining and entertainment, and shopping and leisure, to further examine coordination and response capabilities among various departments. A manager with Adora Cruises said the first trial voyage is an important part of preparations for the ship's maiden voyage, and serves as a real-world test of operational support capabilities, product experience and service procedures. After arriving in Guangzhou, the ship will proceed with preparations for home port berthing, port coordination and maiden voyage service procedures. A second trial voyage is planned for Nov. 14-16, and the ship will launch its inaugural season from Guangzhou on Nov. 22. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: How Xi steers China's green transformation and global climate action
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
How Xi steers China's green transformation and global climate action Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, plants a tree during a voluntary tree-planting activity at Baishan Town in Changping District of Beijing, capital of China, March 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- In 2026, the intensifying fallout of global climate change -- manifesting in catastrophic flooding, rampant wildfires, and record heatwaves -- reaffirms the imperative for immediate, coordinated global action. With global climate tipping points looming, the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), set to kick off on Monday in Antalya, Türkiye, will offer a new opportunity for the international community to renew momentum for more effective global climate cooperation. Under the leadership of President Xi Jinping, China has over the years stayed committed to advancing ecological protection and green transition domestically, and promoting international climate cooperation, making major global contributions to the world's fight against what many regard as an existential threat to humanity. "LIKE WE PROTECT OUR EYES" "We should protect the environment like we protect our eyes." This evocative principle -- voiced on various occasions by Xi -- frames ecological conservation not merely as a policy choice, but as a vital imperative drawn directly from his own experiences. "Over four decades ago, I lived and worked for many years in a small village on the Loess Plateau in western China," Xi recalled in reply to a letter from student representatives of the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate in 2020. Back then, the ecology and environment there was seriously damaged due to over-development, and the local people were trapped in poverty as a result. That experience has taught him that man and nature are a community of life and that the damage done to nature will ultimately hurt humanity. An avid reader of Chinese classics, Xi has also been deeply influenced by the traditional Chinese philosophy that views man as an integral part of nature. "All beings flourish when they live in harmony and receive nourishment from nature," he has said. This conviction underpins the signature environmental doctrine that "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets," which Xi first introduced in 2005 while serving as Party chief of east China's Zhejiang Province. Upon becoming General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee in 2012, Xi made ecological conservation a national priority. An aerial drone photo taken on June 3, 2024 shows the scenery of the Fenhe River in Taiyuan, north China's Shanxi Province. (Xinhua/Yang Chenguang) For Xi, ecological conservation requires not only a profound shift in development philosophy, but also robust institutional safeguards. As he has put it, "Eco-environmental protection relies on laws and regulations." At his direction, environmental performance has become a key criterion for evaluating officials, while environmental inspections have reinforced local governments' accountability for fulfilling their environmental responsibilities. Together, these measures have helped steer China's economic growth toward a more resource-efficient and sustainable path. Since 2012, China has sustained a 6 percent average annual economic growth rate while capping an average energy consumption increase to just 3.3 percent. This structural decoupling yielded a 26.1 percent cumulative decline in energy intensity, marking one of the steepest efficiency gains globally. Xi has also led by example in promoting environmental protection and green development. Since becoming China's top leader, he has personally participated in tree-planting activities in Beijing for 14 consecutive years. Forests have the capacity to conserve water, bring in economic benefits, and boost grain production, and now serve well as a carbon sink, he has noted. Today, China has expanded its forest coverage to over 25 percent of its land area, planting trees across an area roughly 1.7 times the size of California since 2012. The annual carbon-sink capacity of China's forests and grassland has exceeded 1.2 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalents. Fuad Gani, vice director of the Graduate School of Sustainable Development at the University of Indonesia, said that China's ecological conservation philosophy stands out for its ability to translate environmental goals into long-term policies and governance frameworks. "It is one of China's most valuable contributions to advancing green transformation on the global stage," he said. An aerial drone photo taken on July 29, 2025 shows photovoltaic panels at the site of a desertification control project integrated with wind and solar power facilities in Horqin Right Wing Middle Banner of Hinggan League, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Ding He) "SOMETHING WE MUST DO OURSELVES" Balancing economic growth with green development remains a challenge for economies worldwide, especially emerging markets seeking to meet development needs while pursuing environmental sustainability. In Xi's view, economic growth and the green transition are not opposing forces, but complementary goals. This philosophy is captured in his defining doctrine -- "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets." Achieving China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, Xi has stressed, "is not something that others ask us to do, but something we must do ourselves." Under his leadership, China has effectively aligned emissions reduction with technological innovation, industrial upgrading and energy security, turning the green transition into an increasingly important driver of high-quality development. As early as 2014, when conventional gasoline-powered vehicles still dominated China's roads, Xi recognized the enormous potential of new energy vehicles (NEVs). During an inspection tour of SAIC Motor, a major Chinese carmaker, Xi depicted developing NEVs as the only way for China to move from a major automobile country to an automobile powerhouse. In the following decade, the president has demonstrated consistent support for electric cars, visiting automotive companies, touring laboratories, and showing great interest in trying new home-developed models. China's NEV industry has since grown rapidly, emerging as a flagship of the country's technology-intensive manufacturing sector. Beyond the NEV sector, China has also built the world's largest and most comprehensive clean energy industrial chain, with green and low-carbon industries emerging as an important engine of economic growth. The growing exports of the "new three" -- photovoltaic products, lithium-ion batteries and electric vehicles -- are a testament to China's successful shift toward innovation-driven manufacturing. Beyond its own borders, China is now channeling this green innovation momentum into regional cooperation. Customers view a Chinese-brand electric car in Jakarta, Indonesia, June 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Cen Yunpeng) China will continue to work with fellow Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) countries to increase the installed capacity of photovoltaic and wind power each by 10 million kilowatts, and nurture more green industry talents through China-SCO cooperation, said Xi at the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the SCO this September. China's exports of solar panels, wind turbines, electric vehicles and batteries this year will help the world to avoid 450 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, according to a recent analysis by the Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air. The development exemplifies China's strategic push to cultivate "new quality productive forces" -- a policy concept first articulated by Xi in 2023 to drive high-tech innovation and sustainable economic modernization. "Green development," as Xi once put it, "is the defining feature of high-quality development, and new quality productive forces are green in nature." China has turned the challenges of addressing climate change into opportunities for technological innovation, industrial upgrading and high-quality economic development, said Wang Lei, a professor at the School of Government of Beijing Normal University. "Guided by the goals of reducing carbon emissions and strengthening climate resilience, the country has leveraged policy guidance, market incentives and open innovation to drive the transformation of energy, industry, transportation and construction," he added. Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a speech at the opening ceremony of the United Nations (UN) climate change conference in Paris, France, Nov. 30, 2015. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) "EXTREME RESOLUTIONS" Deeply committed to joining world nations to build a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi has repeatedly called on the international community to strengthen cooperation in addressing climate change and actively advanced the building of a fair and equitable global climate governance system for win-win cooperation. "Supreme resources spring from extreme resolutions," Xi said, invoking a perceptive line from French writer Victor Hugo's Les Miserables during his address to the historic 2015 Paris climate change conference. During the summit, Xi put forward important ideas and proposals and worked actively to build consensus among parties, making an indispensable contribution to the eventual adoption of the Paris Agreement. At a special ceremony on Sept. 3, 2016, Xi solemnly handed over China's instrument of joining the Paris Agreement to then UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon. "Had not been President Xi Jinping's initiative, we would not have the Paris Agreement on climate change even now," Ban said in a 2021 interview with Xinhua. In response to the grave challenge of climate change, China has taken on its international responsibilities with what Xi described as "extreme resolutions." At a virtual UN gathering in 2020, Xi announced that China would strive to peak carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. In 2021, he pledged that China would not build new coal-fired power projects abroad. In recent years, some developed countries, particularly those in the West, have backtracked on their climate commitments, undermining global climate governance. Against this backdrop, Xi announced China's 2035 Nationally Determined Contributions in 2025, including a commitment to reduce economy-wide net greenhouse gas emissions by 7-10 percent from peak levels and to raise the share of non-fossil fuels in total energy consumption to more than 30 percent by 2035. For the first time, China committed to absolute emissions reduction targets covering all economic sectors and all greenhouse gases, providing much-needed certainty and stability for global climate governance. Xi has also emphasized the need to uphold fairness and equity and fully respect developing countries' right to development as the world pursues a green transition. "The transition should serve to narrow rather than widen the North-South gap," he said, urging developed countries to take the lead in fulfilling emissions reduction obligations and provide more financial and technological support to developing countries. Under Xi's leadership, China has been striving to strengthen South-South cooperation on climate change. Xi has proposed the establishment of the Belt and Road Initiative International Green Development Coalition and advocated building a green BRICS partnership. Through these target-driven initiatives, China seeks to deepen cooperation in clean energy, green technology and green industrial development, while helping developing countries strengthen their capacity to address climate change. "The Earth is our one and only home," Xi has said. "To scale up efforts to address climate change and promote sustainable development bears on the future of humanity."
